messages:
maria-sales: Heads-up 10x bank wants a committed plan. They expect steady 1.8k RPS for core flows with flash bursts to 4.8k for up to 45s. Requirements: p95 < 350ms, customer-managed KMS, and a pricing appendix for reserved + burst. Can we sketch a proposal?

lee-se: Need token distribution. If payloads are tiny we can get a lot of req/s per GPU; long completions change the math. Also ask about embeddings vs. chat mix.

ida-ml: Baseline numbers: with model rdx-gptx-large-4q our bench shows ~420 tokens/s per A100-80GB equiv when using our quantized path. For short 20-token roundtrips that's ~21 req/s/GPU.

maria-sales: Customer update: ~65% short chat (avg 18 tokens total), 25% embeddings small vectors, 10% rerank. So effective avg ~20 tokens/request.

ida-ml: Recalc: 420 / 20 = 21 req/s per GPU. So for 1,800 RPS baseline -> ~86 GPUs. For 4,800 RPS burst -> ~229 GPUs. Big difference vs earlier guess.

tonya-ops: Ops notes: spinning 200+ GPUs on demand has startup latency and cost. Recommend reserved baseline 90 GPUs across 3 AZs, plus a hybrid burst strategy: small warm standby (12 nodes per AZ) + fast autoscale pool up to 230 GPUs using a mix of on-demand and spot. Warm nodes keep models loaded to cut cold-start. Scale-down cooldown should be 45s to avoid flapping.

nina-security: KMS: they insist on CMK. Hosted offering can support envelope encryption with customer CMK but requires encrypt-in-transit controls and a legal addendum. Private deployment is simpler. I'll draft the questionnaire response and flag the hosted KMS caveat.

lee-se: Fallback plan for capacity shortfall: route traffic to a smaller quantized model (rdx-gptx-medium-4q) and return a degrade signal in response headers. Define SLA exception when fallback happens. Also add per-route rate limits and a retry-with-backoff guidance for client.

infra-bot: warm-pool-requested: 36 nodes across az-1/az-2/az-3 created (placeholder).

ida-ml: Latency note: p95 is dominated by queueing when utilization >75%. With 90 GPUs baseline and warm pool + AZ spread, expected p95 under baseline should be within 200-300ms for these tiny requests. We'll still run a trace-driven sim once they share logs.

tonya-ops: I'll draft the autoscale rules for the proposal: triggers: queue_depth > 120 for 8s OR p95 latency > 260ms -> scale up steps: +10% capacity per 15s up to on-demand limit, then burst to spot. Scale-in: cooldown 45s, aggressive drain policy for spot evictions. Add manual runbook to flip routing to compact model.

maria-sales: Pricing ask: they want reserved monthly price and burst credits pricing. Suggest we present three tiers: (1) Reserved baseline (90 GPUs) flat monthly; (2) Burst credits pool (pre-purchased hours for spot/on-demand); (3) Overage per-GPU on-demand at higher rate.

nina-security: Also callout: audit logs + KMS key usage logs required for compliance. Hosted can provide logs but retention and access controls must be agreed.

lee-se: Action list: 1) Customer sends 48h trace (maria). 2) ida runs sim to produce GPU counts and p95 projections. 3) tonya writes autoscale + warm-pool runbook and cost estimate. 4) nina completes security questionnaire entries for KMS/audit logs and lists hosted blockers. 5) sales to produce a 3-tier price sheet with a fallback SLA note.

maria-sales: On it 1 I'll get the trace and schedule a follow-up in 48h. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
